codeReview.summary: Reviewed commit 3c4bfa6b (22 files, +10,988/-260) against VAL-BOOK-001..022/034/036/037, VAL-GUEST-022/025 and VAL-HOST-005..012/017..020, and re-checked the current combined tree (HEAD 403e6c0c) where a later feature consumes this backend. What is solid: the day feed's composite ETag plus short ETag, 304 handling and /changes polling; withReservationWrite (exclusive run, busy retry, idempotency replay/conflict with request hash, day-version bump, SQLite constraint mapping); expectedVersion -> 409 stale_version on every reservation mutation; audited overbooking with a required reason and a PII-free audit payload; engine reflow that refuses locked/arrived/seated/inside-freeze bookings and returns moves[] with fromTableIds/toTableIds; guest export sensitive gating with guest.export/guest.erase audits and full erase redaction ({redacted:true}); location-scoped token enforcement (403 location_forbidden); the dynamic security sweep over every mounted operator route (missing/forged token, wrong audience/typ/TTL, region mismatch, grantless, wrong scope, impersonated write, unprovisioned 404, cross-org, excluded locationIds); the real-SQLite last-table race (1 winner, 9x409) with idempotent replay; section-layout CRUD with table_in_multiple_sections (409); and the App region-summary counts route. Fail because approved requirements are unmet: the location-delete guard cannot work against the /location-summary response this feature added; GET /book/conflicts and GET /reservations/:id/events do not exist; actual covers cannot be set through the status API (covers_actual and rsv_guests.covers end up as party size, not the passed value); contact_statuses_enabled / course_statuses_enabled are never enforced; the reflow event is written as table_changed instead of the required auto_reassigned; the service-notes expectedVersion is accepted but ignored; and the extended seed silently drops five fields (empty pre-service note body, section sort all 0, NULL arrived/seated covers and notes) because it uses column names that do not exist and Drizzle ignores unknown keys.

issues.description: The demo seed data this feature added is silently dropped because five object keys are not real Drizzle columns: `sortOrder` (should be `sort`) at 985, 997, 1005, 1013, 1031; `notes`/`updatedByUserId` (should be `body`/`updatedBy`) at 1082-1084; and `arrivedPartySize`/`guestNotes`/`internalNotes` (should be `arrivedCovers`/`guestRequests`/`staffNotes`) at 1106, 1111-1112, 1123, 1128-1129, 1145-1146, 1157, 1163, 1174, 1241, 1247-1248, and again in the `onConflictDoUpdate.set` at 1265, 1269-1270. Drizzle 0.45.2 builds inserts and conflict-update SET clauses by iterating the table's columns (node_modules/drizzle-orm/sqlite-core/dialect.cjs:84-102), so unknown keys are ignored with no error, and apps/tenant-api/tsconfig.json only includes src/** and workers/**, so scripts/ is never typechecked. Verified read-only in the seeded tenant DBs: rsv_service_notes.body = '' with updated_by NULL, rsv_sections.sort = 0 for all three sections, and every seeded reservation has NULL arrived_covers/seated_covers/guest_requests/staff_notes. The feature description explicitly includes 'seed:reservations demo guests/bookings', so the demo pre-service note renders blank on the Overview screen and the intended '3 of 6 waiting at bar' / 'Birthday celebration' demo fields never exist.

POST /internal/reservations/location-summary is registered as an alias of /summary (both call handleInternalSummary at 115-140), so it returns the org-wide shape from getRegionalReservationSummary (apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-day-feed-service.ts:1629-1642: activeLocations, reservations, upcomingReservations, guests, tables, auditEntries, activeWaitlist, activeHolds, byLocation) and never a top-level `locationId` or `futureReservations`. The consumer added in the same commit, fetchLocationReservationsSummary (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/region-guard.server.ts:60-70), parses the response with locationReservationsSummarySchema (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/region-confirmation.ts:35-43), which requires both fields, and treats a parse failure as 'regional service unreachable', returning 503. Result: checkLocationReservationsDeleteGuard (region-guard.server.ts:91-140) can never return the 409/200 paths for a provisioned org - location deletion is always blocked with 'Could not reach the regional reservation service' (VAL-BOOK-031). The App unit test passes only because it mocks the tenant-api response with the expected shape (apps/app/app/routes/_app+/$orgSlug_+/settings+/locations.reservations-guard.test.ts:101-114); no test exercises the real /location-summary shape. Fix either side: return { locationId, futureReservations, activeFutureReservations, activeWaitlist, activeHolds, tables, canDelete } from /location-summary, or derive it from byLocation in the guard.

GET /operator/reservations/book/conflicts (architecture.md:1352, VAL-BOOK-012) is not implemented. The full registration block (lines 164-1404) has /day, /changes, /availability, /calendar, /overview, /service-notes, /section-assignments, /sections/assignments, /guests/lookup, /guests/:id/summary, /reservations, /walk-ins, /reservations/:id (GET/PATCH), /assign, /status, /undo, /contact, /running-late, /course, /notes - no /conflicts. Nothing server-side produces a conflicts payload either: rsv-day-feed-service.ts has no conflict handling and the App computes the Unassigned & Conflict panel client-side from the day feed (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/book-api.ts:1266-1297). VAL-BOOK-012's pass condition and its network evidence (GET /operator/reservations/book/conflicts -> 200) therefore cannot be satisfied.

GET /operator/reservations/book/reservations/:id/events (architecture.md:1349, VAL-BOOK-013) is not implemented; the only GET on that path is the detail route at 964. Events are returned inline by getReservationDetail (apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-booking-service.ts:1266-1299 returns `events` with the reservation), which is why the App's detail sheet works (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/book-api.ts:1979-1990 reads raw.events), but VAL-BOOK-013 requires the dedicated endpoint and its network evidence (GET .../reservations/:id/events -> 200). A curl to that path currently falls through to Hono's 404.

Actual covers cannot be set through the status endpoint (VAL-BOOK-017). statusTransitionSchema accepts only `coversActual` (1121-1133) and the handler forwards `...parsed.data` unchanged (1164), while transitionReservationStatus reads `seatedPartySize`/`seatedCovers`/`arrivedPartySize`/`arrivedCovers` and has no `coversActual` input (apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-booking-service.ts:2237-2246). The contract's payload `covers: 4` is stripped by Zod (unknown key), and `coversActual: 4` is accepted but dead, so seatedCovers falls back to current.seatedCovers ?? arrivedCovers ?? current.partySize (2298-2303): `covers_actual` is stored as the party size and rsv_guests.covers is incremented by party size (2343-2348) instead of the passed 4. The worker's own test hides this by calling the service directly with seatedPartySize (apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-booking-service.test.ts:676), and the App client never sends covers either (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/book-api.ts:2410-2431), so there is no path anywhere that records actual covers.

contact_statuses_enabled and course_statuses_enabled are never enforced (VAL-BOOK-022; VAL-BOOK-023 is the UI feature's but the gate belongs here). updateReservationContactStatus only checks that the status is pre-arrival (2749-2754) and updateReservationCourseStatus only checks `seated` (2961-2966); the settings are written by setup (apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-setup-service.ts:587-591) but no booking-service code reads them (grep for contactStatusesEnabled/courseStatusesEnabled finds only setup routes/service). On the seeded acme location (contact_statuses_enabled = 1, course_statuses_enabled = 0) turning the setting off still lets POST /contact and POST /course return 200 and append contact_status/course events, where VAL-BOOK-022 requires 409/400 once contact_statuses_enabled = 0.

Soft reflow writes event type `table_changed` with data.reason='reflow' (1663-1677; the swap path at 1537-1551 also writes `table_changed`) instead of the canonical `auto_reassigned` that architecture.md:789-791 lists and VAL-HOST-008 requires ('records an auto_reassigned event on R1', evidence sqlite(rsv_reservation_events auto_reassigned)). The string `auto_reassigned` appears nowhere in the code (grep over apps and packages), so the assertion's sqlite evidence fails even though the behavior itself works: R1 is reflowed inside the same transaction and moves[] carries reservationId/fromTableIds/toTableIds (1679-1690).

upsertServiceNotes declares `expectedVersion` (1292) and the route forwards it (apps/tenant-api/src/routes/operator-reservations-book.ts:472, 512), but the function never compares it to the stored rsv_service_notes.version before updating (1295-1339), so a stale write silently overwrites another operator's shift notes instead of returning 409 stale_version. This violates the mission write-path rule 'Every operator mutation sends and checks expectedVersion' and contradicts the worker's own handoff ('service-notes with expectedVersion (409 stale_version)') and the library note it added. Related: putSectionAssignments (1400-1467) performs an unversioned delete+insert with no expectedVersion parameter at all. No assertion covers staleness for these two endpoints, which is why the worker's tests pass.

The route-local parseBody/parseQuery helpers (90-122 and 124-150) always include Zod's `issue.message`, while the shared helper suppresses messages for echoing codes (apps/tenant-api/src/lib/http.ts:19-43, ECHOING_CODES = invalid_enum_value/invalid_literal/invalid_union/invalid_union_discriminator). The book router validates enums (assignment at 797/1015/1077, channel/source at 815-816), so a rejected value such as an invalid channel is echoed back as "Invalid enum value. Expected 'host' | 'phone' | 'online' | 'walk_in', received '...'", against the mission rule 'Validation errors never echo rejected values'. The worker's test only covers a regex case (apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-book.test.ts:536-548), and the same helper copy exists in operator-reservations-guests.ts:24-83. Using readJsonBody/readQuery (or ECHOING_CODES) fixes it.

handlePutSectionAssignments calls putSectionAssignments without `actorId` (666-677) although the service supports it (apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-day-feed-service.ts:1406) and writes it to the audit row (1445-1459). Every `section_assignment.put` rsv_audit_log row therefore has actorId NULL, unlike the section-layout audits which pass ctx.userId. Pass actorId: ctx.userId for traceability.

Path naming drift to reconcile in the mission docs: the validation contract and architecture.md:1348 name POST /reservations/:id/contact-status and /course-status, but this implementation registers /contact (1225) and /course (1320) - matching the feature's own expectedBehavior and the App client (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/book-api.ts uses /contact, /running-late, /course). A validator curling the contract paths gets 404, not the documented 200/409. Either add the contract aliases or reconcile architecture.md/validation-contract.md with the shipped paths so the two documents do not contradict each other.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The library section this worker added to library/staffing-patterns.md documents behavior that does not exist: it says `GET/PUT/POST /service-notes` has `expectedVersion` (409 `stale_version`), but upsertServiceNotes never checks it. Later workers and validators will trust this line. If the fix feature adds the check, the note becomes true; otherwise the note must be corrected.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: library/staffing-patterns.md, 'Reservations Book, Host Stand & Guest Backend Notes' bullet for /service-notes vs apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-day-feed-service.ts:1281-1339 (no version comparison) and apps/tenant-api/src/routes/operator-reservations-book.ts:472,512 (field forwarded).

sharedStateObservations.observation: backend-worker step 7 says to extend seed:reservations 'through the same services as the API', but the reservations seed has always used raw Drizzle inserts, and apps/tenant-api/tsconfig.json includes only src/** and workers/** - so scripts/seed-reservations.ts is never typechecked and Drizzle silently ignores unknown object keys in both .values() and onConflictDoUpdate.set. The worker's verification was count-based ('8 tags, 1 section layout, ... 7 reservations'), which cannot catch wrong column names. The skill (or library/environment.md) should require spot-checking seeded field values with sqlite3, or moving seed inserts through typed helpers.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript: three Execute calls 'Run seed:reservations twice on acme and riyadh-grill to verify idempotency' with count-only observations; apps/tenant-api/scripts/seed-reservations.ts:985,1082-1084,1106,1241,1265; node_modules/drizzle-orm/sqlite-core/dialect.cjs:84-102; apps/tenant-api/tsconfig.json include list.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The new reservations routers copy a local parseBody/parseQuery that echoes Zod messages, while the shared helpers in src/lib/http.ts deliberately suppress messages for echoing codes. Nothing in the mission AGENTS.md or library points at readJsonBody/readQuery or ECHOING_CODES, so every new backend worker re-invents the weaker helper (it also exists in operator-reservations-guests.ts). Adding one line to the library's 'Gotchas' ('errors never echo values: use readJsonBody/readQuery, or ECHOING_CODES') would make the existing rule actionable.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: apps/tenant-api/src/routes/operator-reservations-book.ts:90-150 vs apps/tenant-api/src/lib/http.ts:19-43; enums at operator-reservations-book.ts:797,815-816; the worker's own negative test only covers a date regex (reservations-book.test.ts:536-548).

sharedStateObservations.observation: Cross-feature integration contract for the location-delete guard is not written down: the backend owns /internal/reservations/location-summary, the App owns the guard schema that consumes it, and the two shipped in different commits with incompatible shapes. The library's internal-summary bullet lists only 'POST /internal/reservations/summary' and the App region-summary route, so nothing records what /location-summary must return. Add the exact response contract (locationId, futureReservations, activeFutureReservations, activeWaitlist, activeHolds, tables, canDelete) to the library so the next worker can keep the two sides aligned.

Mission documents disagree on three book-stand endpoints, which makes it ambiguous whether the backend or the contract is wrong: architecture.md/validation-contract require GET /conflicts, GET /reservations/:id/events and /contact-status//course-status, while the feature's expectedBehavior and the App client use /contact and /course and load events inline. Either the docs should be reconciled or the endpoints added; recording the decision in the library prevents the next feature from re-litigating it.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: architecture.md:1348-1352; validation-contract.md VAL-BOOK-012/013/022/023; apps/tenant-api/src/routes/operator-reservations-book.ts route list (164-1404); apps/app/app/utils/reservations/book-api.ts:2410 (status path) and 1979-1990 (events inline).

summary: Reviewed foh-book-and-host-backend (commit 3c4bfa6b, worker 72033e19, backend-worker skill, no skillFeedback deviations reported) against its 39 fulfilled assertions, reading the full booking/day-feed/guest services and routes, the security sweep, the concurrency test, the seed script and the current combined tree (HEAD 403e6c0c). Verdict: fail. The core write path is strong - withReservationWrite with idempotency replay/conflict, expectedVersion -> 409 stale_version on every reservation mutation, composite ETag + 304 and /changes polling, audited overbooking with a required reason and no PII, reflow that refuses locked/arrived/seated/inside-freeze bookings and returns moves[], guest export/erase with audits and full redaction, dynamic per-route security sweep, and a real-SQLite last-table race test - but eight approved requirements are unmet: (1) the extended seed writes five fields under non-existent column names, so the demo pre-service note is empty, section sort is 0 and seeded reservations lose arrived/seated covers and notes (Drizzle silently drops unknown keys; scripts/ is outside tsconfig); (2) /internal/reservations/location-summary returns the org-wide shape while the App's location-delete guard requires { locationId, futureReservations }, so the guard always answers 503 (VAL-BOOK-031); (3) GET /book/conflicts is missing (VAL-BOOK-012); (4) GET /reservations/:id/events is missing (VAL-BOOK-013); (5) `covers`/`coversActual` never reach the transition service, so covers_actual and rsv_guests.covers use the party size instead of the passed value (VAL-BOOK-017); (6) contact_statuses_enabled/course_statuses_enabled are never enforced (VAL-BOOK-022, VAL-BOOK-023); (7) reflow writes table_changed instead of the required auto_reassigned event (VAL-HOST-008); (8) service-notes expectedVersion is accepted but ignored (mission write-path directive; also unversioned section-assignment PUT). Non-blocking: route-local validation echoes rejected enum values, section-assignment audits have actorId null, and the contract/architecture names (/contact-status, /course-status) differ from the shipped /contact and /course paths. Suggested validator spot-checks: sqlite3 the seeded tenant DB for rsv_service_notes.body/rsv_sections.sort/arrived_covers; curl /internal/reservations/location-summary and compare with the App guard schema; curl GET /operator/reservations/book/conflicts and .../reservations/<id>/events; POST /status with covers:4 and read rsv_reservations.seated_covers and rsv_guests.covers; set contact_statuses_enabled=0 and call /contact; assign onto an occupied soft table and query rsv_reservation_events for auto_reassigned.
